scenario: In-flight authorization revocation (project-scoped) on an isolated acceptance database

environment.deterministicDelay: [[delay-decision-ms:30000]] armed by an ANSWER_TIP free text (engine=fake only)

productPathUsed.note: the UI/API revocation path was used, not a raw DB write; the removal happened ~5.1s after the answer run started, while it was still in flight (phase DECIDING)

defectFound.summary: After the run was terminalized as FAILED (event RUN_FAILED, reason TASK_CANCELLED, at 23:43:00.071), the same cancelled run continued and appended non-terminal events ~25.6s later: PROPOSAL_CREATED, PROCESS_NOTE, EXECUTING, PROCESS_NOTE at 23:43:25.70. The task lease was already revoked and the run already terminal.
defectFound.whyItHappened: The deterministic delay is a plain Thread.sleep that does not observe task cancellation; when it returned, the in-flight answer cycle persisted a REQUEST_USER_INPUT proposal and appended events to an already-terminal run. The equivalent production shape is a long model call returning after cancellation.
defectFound.whyItMatters: This is exactly the late-result-rejection requirement: a terminal run must not accept late non-terminal writes. The persisted event stream diverges from the SSE contract (a client closes on the terminal event and never sees events 8-11); sequence stays contiguous but ordering/closure semantics are violated.
defectFound.needsAudit: Whether the business-cycle event append path is covered by TaskWriteGuard.lockOwnedTask / ExecutionFence for cancelled (not just taken-over) tasks.

otherFinding.summary: DELETE /organizations/{org}/members/{alice} returns a product error: 'The last active OWNER cannot leave the organization'.
otherFinding.implication: Organization-level self-revocation is unreachable for a single-member org; a real in-flight org-scoped revocation acceptance would need a second OWNER/member (and a second identity session). This is a correct fail-closed invariant, not a defect.

limitations: The 30s delay is a test-only deterministic fixture; production timing differs
SSE terminal event was not observed live in this scenario (revocation ends the session and the delay path is the target)
The project f5cd6745-af30-43c3-a6b3-420d96071961 and the earlier 42563250-... were left revoked in the isolated acceptance DB as test artifacts
No DB-outage, slow-client or kill-process takeover acceptance in this scenario
